_Order of the_ THISTLE, or of St ANDREW, a military order of knighthood in Scotland, the rife and institution whereof is varioully related by different authors. Lekey, bithop of Rofs, reports, that the night before the battle between Athelllan king of Northumberland, and Hungus king of the Piets, a bright crofs, in form of that where- on St Andrew (the tutelar faint of Scotland) suffered martyrdom, appeared to Hungus; who having gained the victory, ever after bore the figure of that crols on his banners. Others affert, that Achaius king of Scotland sirft infiltrated this order, after having made the famous league offenfive and definitive with Charlemagne king of France. But although the thiffle had been acknowledged as the fymbol of the kingdom of Scotland from the reign of Achaius, yet fome refer the beginning of this order to Charles VII, of France. Others place the foundation of it as low as the year 1500.

The chief and principal enfign is a gold collar compo- fed of thillles and lprigs of rue interlinked with amulets of gold, having pendent thereunto the image of St Andrew with his crofs, and the motto, NEMO ME IMPUNE LA- CESSET.

The ordinary or common enfign worn by the knights, is a flat of four silver points, and over them a green cir- cle, bordered and lettered with gold, containing the faid motto, and in the centre is a thiffle proper ; all which is embroidered on their left breast, and worn with the collar, with a green ribband over the left shoulder, and brought under the right arm ; pendent thereto is the i- mage of St Andrew, with his crofs, in a purple robe, within an oval of gold enameled vert, with the former motto: but fometimes they wear, encircled in the fame manner, a thiffle crowned.

About the time of the reformation, this order was dropped, till James II. of England refumed it, by crea-ting eight knights: however, the revolution unfettled it again, and it lay neglected till queen Anne, in 1703, restored it to the primitive design, of twelve knights of St Andrew.

THOM EANS, THOMISTS, or _Chritians of St_ THOMAS, a people of the Eaft-Indies, who, according to the tradition, received the Golpel from St Thomas. Upon the arrival of the Portuguese at Calicut, in their first voyage to the Indies, they met with ancient Christians, who pretended to be defended from those converted by St Thomas. The Thomazas being informed of a new people arrived among them, who bore a particular veneration for the

A mix-ture of opinions, with a total interruption of pallors, fometimes for feveral years together,' occaftoned that horrible chaos their religion was in at the arrival of the Portuguese ; for a fpecimen whereof we thall add their manner of celebrating the eucharift: Over their altar was a kind of gallery; and while the prieft was laying the beginning of the office below, a cake of flour of rice was trying in oil, or butter, above ; when enough, the cake was let down in a basket upon the altar, where the priest confecrated it: as to the other species, for wine they ufed a kind of brandy or arrack, varioufly prepared in that country. Nor was their ordination much more regular ; the archdeacon, who was fometimes more rejected than the bithop himself, frequently ordained prietis: their other abufes were infinite. The Portuguese, for thefe two laft centuries, have laboured the reforma-tion of this church, and have employed both the eccle-fialic and fecular power therein : for this end they have called the Thomzan bifhops to the council at Goa, have infruited, charged them, cc, and even fent them for infiltration to Portugal and Rome ; but finding that they were till apt to relapfe at their return, and that no good was like to be done with them, they refolved to exclude them once for all, and to appoint an European bilhop in their room. Thefe proceedings have rendered the Portuguese infinitely odious to the Thomazans.

THOMISM, the doctrine of St Thomas Aquinas, and his followers the Thomifts, chiefly with regard to predeflina-tion and grace. There is fome doubt what the true genuine thomifm is, but there are authors who dliftinguih the thomifm of St Thomas from that of the dominicans. Others again make thomifm no other than a kind of janfenifm dilguifed : but janfenifm, it is known, has been condemned by the popes, which pure thomifm never was: in effect, the writings of Alvarez and Lemos, who were appointed by their order to lay down and defend, before the holy fee, the dogmata of their school, have since been reputed the rule of pure thomifm.
